hasEvidenceItems.description: The provided abstract mentions a MYBPC3 variant in a patient with cardiomyopathy but does not specify the nucleotide or protein change. Therefore, it is impossible to determine if the target variant c.2905+1G>A is the one being discussed.
The paper does not study the target variant c.2905+1G>A; it focuses on a different deep-intronic variant (c.2308+227G>A).

The paper uses multiple functional assays (contractility, calcium handling, and structural organization) in a human iPSC-derived micro-heart tissue model to demonstrate that the MYBPC3fs variant causes hypercontractility, calcium handling abnormalities, and sarcomere disarray. These findings collectively support a damaging functional effect consistent with HCM pathogenesis.

value.detail: Engineered human micro-heart tissue (iPSC-CMs and cFBs), readout: Peak active force, contraction kinetics, and mechanical energy consumption, vs Isogenic control iPSC-CMs - MYBPC3fs tissues exhibited significantly higher peak active force (hypercontractility) under stiff-post loading, especially at higher fibroblast fractions.; Mutant tissues showed faster contraction kinetics and altered energy consumption.

value.message: Calcium imaging: functionally_abnormal
value.detail: Engineered human micro-heart tissue (iPSC-CMs and cFBs), readout: Calcium transient amplitude (ΔF/F), upstroke duration (UPD), and decay time, vs Isogenic control iPSC-CMs - MYBPC3fs tissues showed shorter calcium upstroke duration and altered peak calcium amplitude depending on load and fibroblast density.

value.message: Structural analysis (Immunostaining/Sarcomere organization): functionally_abnormal
value.detail: Engineered human micro-heart tissue (iPSC-CMs and cFBs), readout: Myofibrillar alignment (orientational order parameter) and Z-disk organization, vs Isogenic control iPSC-CMs - MYBPC3fs tissues showed blunted myofibrillar alignment gains and increased sarcomere disorganization (disarray) compared to controls, especially under load and pro-fibrotic (TGF-β) stimulation.
